ASTROHEALTH

A Smart Health Monitoring Application for Astronauts

1. Abstract

Space missions are very challenging because astronauts have to work in an environment that is completely different from Earth. During their missions, they may experience several physical and mental health problems due to microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation, changes in sleep patterns and other environmental conditions.

At present, monitoring the health of astronauts is an important part of space missions. However, continuous health monitoring and early identification of health problems can be improved with the help of smart technology.

This project proposes AstroHealth, a smart health monitoring application designed to monitor the physical and mental health of astronauts during space missions. The application aims to collect health-related information such as heart rate, blood oxygen level, body temperature, sleep patterns and activity levels through wearable devices and sensors.

The collected information will be displayed in a simple dashboard so that astronauts can monitor their health conditions. The application can also identify unusual changes in health parameters and generate alerts when necessary. It will provide basic health suggestions and help astronauts maintain their health throughout the mission.

2. Introduction

Space exploration has become an important part of scientific and technological development. Astronauts spend several days or even months in space, where their bodies experience conditions that are very different from those on Earth.

One of the major challenges faced by astronauts is maintaining their health in microgravity. Microgravity can affect muscle strength, bone density, blood circulation and balance. Apart from physical changes, astronauts may also experience stress, sleep disturbances and psychological difficulties due to isolation and limited communication.

Regular health monitoring is therefore necessary to ensure the safety and performance of astronauts.

Our proposed project, AstroHealth, focuses on developing a digital application that helps astronauts monitor their health in a convenient way. Instead of depending only on periodic medical assessments, the application aims to provide continuous access to important health information and alert users when unusual changes are detected.

3. Problem Statement

Astronauts work in an environment where immediate access to medical facilities and healthcare professionals is limited.

Some health-related problems may develop gradually and may not be noticed immediately. Changes in heart rate, oxygen saturation, sleep quality and physical activity can provide important information about an astronaut's health.

The main problem addressed by this project is the need for an accessible and integrated health monitoring system that can help astronauts identify possible health issues at an early stage.

4. Objectives

The main objectives of the AstroHealth application are:

1. To monitor important health parameters of astronauts.

2. To provide real-time or near-real-time health information through a digital dashboard.

3. To identify unusual changes in health conditions.

4. To generate alerts when health parameters move outside predefined safe limits.

5. To monitor sleep patterns and physical activity.

6. To provide basic health recommendations.

7. To maintain health records throughout the space mission.

8. To support communication of relevant health information to mission medical teams.

5. Proposed System

AstroHealth is proposed as a mobile and tablet-based health monitoring application that can work with wearable sensors.

The system collects health information from connected devices and processes the collected data. The information is then displayed through an easy-to-understand dashboard.

The application will have different sections for physical health, sleep monitoring, activity tracking, mental well-being and emergency alerts.

If any health parameter shows an unusual change, the application will notify the astronaut and can make the relevant information available to the authorised medical team.

The application is intended to support health monitoring and decision-making rather than replace professional medical diagnosis.

6. Main Features

6.1 Real-Time Health Monitoring

The application will monitor important health parameters such as:

- Heart rate

- Blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂)

- Body temperature

- Blood pressure (if supported by the connected device)

- Physical activity levels

6.2 Sleep Monitoring

Astronauts may experience changes in their sleep cycles because of unusual lighting conditions, mission schedules and the space environment.

This feature will track sleep duration and patterns and provide a summary of sleep quality.

6.3 Physical Activity Monitoring

This section will track daily physical activity and exercise routines. Since microgravity can contribute to muscle and bone loss, monitoring exercise activity is important for astronauts.

6.4 Mental Health and Stress Monitoring

Long-duration missions can affect the psychological well-being of astronauts.

The application can include a daily mood check-in, stress-level questionnaire and basic relaxation suggestions.

6.5 Smart Alerts

The application will generate notifications when monitored health parameters show unusual readings.

For example, if the astronaut's heart rate or oxygen saturation moves outside their personalised safe range, the application can generate an alert.

6.6 Health History and Reports

The application will maintain health records over time. Astronauts and authorised medical professionals can use these records to understand changes in health conditions throughout the mission.

6.7 Emergency Support

In case of a possible medical emergency, the application will provide an emergency alert interface that allows the astronaut to access relevant health information and notify the mission medical team.

7. Working Principle

The proposed application works through the following steps:

1. Data Collection: Wearable sensors collect health-related information from the astronaut.

2. Data Transfer: The collected information is transferred to the application through a connected device.

3. Data Processing: The application analyses the collected readings and compares them with personalised reference limits.

4. Health Dashboard: The processed information is displayed in a simple graphical format.

5. Alert Generation: If unusual readings are detected, the application generates an alert.

6. Health Recommendations: The application provides relevant basic suggestions based on the available information.

7. Data Storage: Health records are stored securely for future monitoring and analysis.

8. Technologies Proposed

The following technologies can be considered for developing the application:

- Frontend: Flutter or React Native for developing the mobile application.

- Backend: Python for processing and analysing health data.

- Database: Firebase or a suitable secure database for storing health records.

- Sensors: Wearable health monitoring devices.

- Data Analysis: Basic machine learning or rule-based algorithms for identifying unusual health patterns.

- UI/UX Design: Figma for designing the application interface.

These technologies are proposed options and can be modified depending on the available resources and project requirements.

9. Expected Outcomes

The expected outcome of this project is a user-friendly health monitoring application that helps astronauts keep track of their health during space missions.

The application is expected to:

- Provide a single platform for viewing important health information.

- Help identify unusual changes in health parameters.

- Improve awareness of physical and mental well-being.

- Maintain health records throughout the mission.

- Support astronauts and medical teams in monitoring health conditions.

10. Future Scope

The application can be improved in several ways in the future.

Advanced machine learning models can be introduced to identify possible health risks by analysing long-term health data. Integration with more wearable sensors can improve the amount of information collected.

The application can also be developed to work with limited or delayed internet connectivity, which is particularly important during space missions.

In the future, the system could be extended to include personalised health monitoring, advanced medical assistance and integration with spacecraft health management systems.

11. Conclusion

AstroHealth is a proposed smart health monitoring application designed to address one of the important challenges of human space exploration: maintaining astronaut health.

By combining wearable sensors, data analysis and a simple application interface, the project aims to make health monitoring easier and more accessible during space missions.

The main idea behind this project is that astronauts should be able to understand their health conditions without depending entirely on periodic medical assessments.

Although the proposed application is still a concept and requires further development and validation, it has the potential to become a useful supporting tool for astronaut health management in future space missions.
